analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 13, 2026)
key_insights: Indices were mixed pre-market (SPX +0.0%, NDX -0.5%, RTY +0.4%). Tech lagged as the rotation out of semis and memory continued, while ex-tech cyclicals and RTY broadened. Over 60% of S&P 500 stocks closed higher the prior day despite lower indices.
AI-linked baskets led the prior-day declines: semis (SOXX -2.6%) and memory (DRAM -4.3%). Pre-market: NVDA -0.6%, MU -2.6%, SMCI -1.9%.

JPM's trading desk says Broadcom CEO Hock Tan's comments deepened concerns about AI financing in both debt and equity. He said at a DBS conference panel that financing could become a bigger bottleneck than component shortages, and he questioned frontier lab business models.

Joshua Meyers (JPM TMT specialist) cites additional drivers of the semis/hardware weakness: a weekend sell-side note on powered-shell shortages of as much as 19GW next year and more in 2028, the CXMT '4F2' memory announcement, a low-liquidity holiday session, and Middle East news. Investors are waiting for an expected private frontier lab investor meeting on Wednesday.

Meyers sees the SOX struggling at its 100-day moving average, with rotation into Mag 7 and Internet names. Optical (LITE, COHR, CIEN), memory (especially SNDK) and SMCI were the key questions. TTMI was punished for its capex announcement, the only name with a company-specific reason.

Oil reversed the prior day's gains (WTI -1.8% to $92.05) and global yields fell, but weekend escalation was clear: Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, and Ukraine said Russia kept hitting energy targets despite the announced energy ceasefire. Energy markets have been range-bound recently.
Treasuries rallied with yields down about 2-5bp, led by the 10-year, which sits at 5.194%. DXY fell 30bp. Gold is at $4,181 and silver at $60.46.

Europe: indices higher, led by the UK and Germany. Defensives and rate-sensitive baskets outperformed, while semis and luxury lagged. LVMH reported worse-than-expected earnings on weak Chinese demand. 10-year Gilt and Bund yields fell 5bp and 4bp.

Factor view (Manish): JPM sees tightening macro conditions reflected in the Quality factor (JPQPURE). Beta (JPBPURE), Momentum (JPMPURE) and Semis (JP2SEM) look vulnerable. Semiconductor sentiment is above the 99th percentile. Quality reversed after the 2023 regional bank crisis and the October 2023 dovish Fed shift, so JPM sees meaningful risk of a Quality reversal around CPI and the late-month Fed meeting if the Fed turns dovish.

Q3 2026 earnings expectations (FactSet): revenue growth 12.4%, earnings growth 29.6%, margin 15.0%. Q2 2026 was 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% earnings growth and 17% margin. All 11 sectors are expected to show positive revenue and earnings growth, which has happened once before (Q2 2021).

Earnings-season watch items: (i) breadth, with 57% of the SPX in a bear market (down 20%+ from highs) per Bloomberg while dispersion declines; (ii) whether beats are rewarded, since 1-day reactions to beats were below historical median in 4 of the last 6 reporting periods; (iii) hyperscaler capex, where a cut is seen as highly unlikely in 2026 earnings; (iv) inflation and consumer price sensitivity, with DAL cutting profit guidance on energy prices.

JPM Market Intel remains Tactically Bullish into earnings. The SOX is about 20% off its July lows and about 15% below its June highs. JPM thinks semis can climb the wall of worry on Hynix/Samsung updates and that deteriorating breadth can reverse into and out of earnings season.
Risks flagged: momentum/tech unwind, tech earnings miss, AI credit fears and spread widening, a spike in bond and equity vol, weaker consumer data.

Catalysts: CPI on Oct 14, Retail Sales and PPI on Oct 15, flash PMIs on Oct 23, Fed on Oct 28. The market currently prices a December hike and two hikes in FY27, so dovish inflation prints could remove hike expectations. Strong bank earnings would help restart the cyclicals trade.

Monetization Menu (Oct 12): preference for Tech and some cyclicals, with AI as a globally bullish theme. Focus the COVID Reopening theme on cruise lines, hotels and retailers, given consumer strength and relative insulation from energy prices. Internationally, ex-AI, JPM likes Brazil and Japan.

Earlier menus (Oct 5, Sep 28): Tech stays a core long, but JPM no longer pairs it with an RTY short because of squeeze risk from lower oil and yields, and prefers a derivative expression. Semis and Mag 7 may outperform within tech. Software is a non-consensus bullish play. Banks are favored ex-AI. A US/Iran deal would be the biggest catalyst, squeezing EU and RTY higher.

Sep 21 menu: keep the long Tech vs short RTY pair dollar-neutral or market-neutral. Early in hiking cycles USD tends to be bid and the curve flattens, supporting Secular Growth and MegaCap Tech, and JPM thinks the US can tactically outperform DM. JPM likes Brazil/Latam regardless of the AI view.

MU was -2.6% pre-market as memory weakened on the CXMT 4F2 news and broader worries.
SMCI was -1.9% pre-market and Meyers had no company-specific reason for the repeated decline.
TTMI was punished for its capex announcement.
SNDK was especially weak within memory.
DAL cut profit guidance on energy prices and an unwillingness to pass on costs to consumers.

May join a squeeze but are likely to lag the SPX ex-AI plays.
Slowly gaining traction but remains a non-consensus bullish play.

earnings_insights: FactSet Q3 2026 expectations: 12.4% revenue growth, 29.6% earnings growth, 15.0% margin (estimates, not reported results). Q2 2026 reported: 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% earnings growth, 17% margin.
FactSet estimates: Q4 2026 revenue growth 12.4% and earnings growth 28.0%. FY26 revenue growth 12.5% and EPS growth 32.7%. FY27 revenue growth 9.4% and EPS growth 15.8%.
11 of 11 sectors are expected to show positive revenue and earnings growth for Q3 2026, which has happened only once before (Q2 2021).
Bank earnings begin: Oct 13 C, GS, JPM, WFC, JNJ, DPZ among others. Oct 14 BAC, BLK, MS, PGR, STT. Oct 15 PLD, PNC, SCHW, USB among others. Oct 16 CFG, TFC, TRV.
DAL cut profit guidance on energy prices. LVMH reported worse-than-expected earnings on weak Chinese demand (per CNBC).
In 4 of the last 6 reporting periods, 1-day reactions to beats came in below historical median, with misses punished more than historically.
